01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these is 360 written as a product of powers of its prime factors?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 360 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2³ × 3² × 5. The others multiply to 360 but contain non-primes (10, 45, 60).

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the HCF of 2³ × 3² × 5 and 2² × 3⁴ × 7?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: HCF: primes common to both (2 and 3) to their LOWEST powers: 2² × 3² = 36. Taking the highest powers and every prime gives the LCM instead.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the LCM of 12 and 15?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 12 = 2² × 3, 15 = 3 × 5. LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60. 180 is 12 × 15, a common multiple but not the lowest; 3 is the HCF.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the LCM of 2⁴ × 3 and 2² × 3³ × 5?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: LCM: every prime, highest power: 2⁴, 3³ and 5. Adding the powers (2⁶ × 3⁴) multiplies the numbers together instead; leaving out the 5 misses a prime.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: One light flashes every 8 seconds and another every 12 seconds. They flash together now. After how many seconds do they next flash together?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: The LCM of 8 and 12 is 24. 96 = 8 × 12 is a common multiple but not the first; 4 is the HCF.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these numbers is prime?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 51 = 3 × 17, 57 = 3 × 19 and 91 = 7 × 13. 59 has no factors other than 1 and itself.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify y⁵ × y⁹
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Multiplying powers of the same base: ADD the indices. 5 + 9 = 14.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify (2m³)⁴
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Everything in the bracket is raised to the power 4: 2⁴ = 16 and (m³)⁴ = m¹². 2m¹² forgets the 2; 16m⁷ adds the indices instead of multiplying.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify (m⁴)⁻³
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Power of a power: multiply the indices. 4 × (−3) = −12.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of c⁰ (c ≠ 0)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: c³ ÷ c³ = c⁰ by the index laws, and anything divided by itself is 1.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Write ∛2 as a power of 2
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: A cube root is the power 1/3, because 2^(1/3) × 2^(1/3) × 2^(1/3) = 2¹.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify 12x⁷y² ÷ 4x³y⁵
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Divide the numbers (12 ÷ 4 = 3) and SUBTRACT indices: x⁷⁻³ = x⁴, y²⁻⁵ = y⁻³.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of 25^(−1/2)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Negative index → reciprocal; power 1/2 → square root. 1/√25 = 1/5. A negative index never makes the answer negative, and it is not a multiplier (25 × −1/2).

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of 27^(2/3)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Root first: ∛27 = 3, then square: 3² = 9. 18 comes from 27 × 2/3, which treats the index as a multiplier.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of (16/81)^(−3/4)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Flip for the negative: (81/16)^(3/4). Fourth root: 3/2. Cube: 27/8. 8/27 forgets to flip.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: What is the value of 8^(−2/3)?
9ˣ = 3⁷ × 3. What is the value of x?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Write 9 as 3²: 3²ˣ = 3⁸, so 2x = 8 and x = 4. 8 forgets that 9 is 3².

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: 8 ÷ 2⁷ = 2ⁿ. What is the value of n?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 8 = 2³, so 2³ ÷ 2⁷ = 2³⁻⁷ = 2⁻⁴. n = 4 subtracts the wrong way round.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these is √72 written in its simplest form?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Take out the LARGEST square factor: 72 = 36 × 2, so √72 = 6√2. 2√18 and 3√8 are equal to √72 but not fully simplified.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Simplify √48 + √27
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: √48 = 4√3 and √27 = 3√3, so the sum is 7√3. √48 + √27 is NOT √75: roots don't add like that (√75 = 5√3).

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out √5 × √20
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: √5 × √20 = √100 = 10. √25 adds the numbers under the root instead of multiplying them.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Expand and simplify (3 + √5)²
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: (3 + √5)(3 + √5) = 9 + 3√5 + 3√5 + 5 = 14 + 6√5. Just squaring each term (9 + 5) misses the two middle terms.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Expand and simplify (2 + √3)(2 − √3)
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Difference of two squares: 2² − (√3)² = 4 − 3 = 1. The surd terms +2√3 and −2√3 cancel.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Rationalise the denominator of 10/√5
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Multiply top and bottom by √5: 10√5/5 = 2√5.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: To rationalise the denominator of 4/(3 − √5), you multiply the top and bottom by…
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Use the denominator with the sign flipped: (3 − √5)(3 + √5) = 9 − 5 = 4, a whole number. Multiplying by (3 − √5) leaves a surd.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Write 4/(3 − √5) in the form a + √b
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 4(3 + √5)/(9 − 5) = 4(3 + √5)/4 = 3 + √5. Dividing by 14 comes from adding 9 + 5 instead of subtracting.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these is a surd?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: √16 = 4, √0.25 = 0.5 and ∛27 = 3 are all rational. √12 = 2√3 is irrational, so it is a surd.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these numbers is irrational?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Recurring decimals and fractions are rational, and √9 = 3. √2 cannot be written as a fraction of integers.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Write 0.00052 in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Move the decimal point 4 places to get 5.2, which lies between 1 and 10. The number is small, so the power is negative: 10⁻⁴. 52 × 10⁻⁵ has A bigger than 10.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out (4.2 × 10⁵) × (3 × 10⁻⁸), giving your answer in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 4.2 × 3 = 12.6 and 10⁵ × 10⁻⁸ = 10⁻³, giving 12.6 × 10⁻³. That is not in standard form, so adjust to 1.26 × 10⁻².

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out (1.2 × 10⁷) ÷ (4.8 × 10³), giving your answer in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: 1.2 ÷ 4.8 = 0.25 and 10⁷ ÷ 10³ = 10⁴, giving 0.25 × 10⁴ = 2.5 × 10³. When A gets 10 times bigger, the power goes DOWN by 1.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Work out 3.2 × 10⁵ + 4.5 × 10⁴, giving your answer in standard form
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Match the powers: 3.2 × 10⁵ + 0.45 × 10⁵ = 3.65 × 10⁵ (320 000 + 45 000 = 365 000). You cannot add the front numbers when the powers differ.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which of these numbers is written in standard form?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: Standard form is A × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ A < 10 and n an integer. 34 and 0.34 are outside that range, and 0.5 is not an integer.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: A calculator shows 2.52E−03. How should the answer be written?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: E−03 means × 10⁻³. The E notation is not accepted on the answer line, so write it in full.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.4545… (45 recurring)?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: x = 0.4545…, 100x = 45.4545…, so 99x = 45 and x = 45/99 = 5/11. 45/100 is 0.45 exactly, which does not recur.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.1444… (4 recurring)?
To write 0.245245… (245 recurring) as a fraction, x is multiplied by which number before subtracting x?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: The repeating block has 3 digits, so use 1000x = 245.245…; then 999x = 245.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.2727… (27 recurring)?
(3 + √x)² = y + 6√2, where x and y are positive integers. Find x and y.
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: (3 + √x)² = 9 + 6√x + x. Matching the surd parts: 6√x = 6√2, so x = 2. Then y = 9 + 2 = 11.

01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.q: The HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. What is their LCM?
01-number-indices-surds-standard-form.explain: HCF × LCM = the product of the two numbers, so LCM = 18 × 24 ÷ 6 = 72. 432 is the product itself.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Work out 3 2/5 − 1 3/4
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 17/5 − 7/4 = 68/20 − 35/20 = 33/20 = 1 13/20. Subtracting whole numbers (2) and then fractions needs care: 2/5 − 3/4 is negative (−7/20).

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Work out 2 1/3 ÷ 1 5/9
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 7/3 ÷ 14/9 = 7/3 × 9/14 = 63/42 = 3/2. 3 17/27 multiplies by 14/9 without flipping it.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: What single number do you multiply by to increase an amount by 15%?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 100% + 15% = 115% = 1.15. 0.15 gives just the increase; 0.85 is a 15% DEcrease.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: What single number do you multiply by to decrease an amount by 7.5%?
A price rises from $480 to $552. What is the percentage increase?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Change = 72. 72 ÷ 480 (the ORIGINAL) × 100 = 15%. Dividing by 552 gives 13.0%.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: After a 12% increase a laptop costs $1344. What was the price before the increase?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Original × 1.12 = 1344, so original = 1344 ÷ 1.12 = 1200. Taking 12% off 1344 (× 0.88) gives 1182.72, which is wrong because the 12% was of the original.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: After an 8% pay rise, Mia earns $32 400. What did she earn before the rise?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 32 400 ÷ 1.08 = 30 000. 32 400 × 0.92 = 29 808 takes 8% of the NEW salary, the error that scored M0 M0 A0 in 2018.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: In a 35% sale, a coat costs $91. What was the price before the sale?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Sale price = 65% of the original, so 91 ÷ 0.65 = 140. 91 × 0.65 and 91 × 1.35 apply the percentage to the wrong amount.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A 15% reduction takes $22.50 off the normal price of a mixer. What is the normal price?
$25 000 is invested at 3.5% per year compound interest. What is it worth after 4 years, to the nearest cent?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 25 000 × 1.035⁴ = 28 688.08. $28 500 is SIMPLE interest (3.5% × 4 = 14%). $3688.08 is only the interest.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A boat loses 4% of its value each year. Which calculation gives its value after 3 years, starting from V?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Each year multiplies by 0.96, so 3 years is × 0.96³. × 0.88 is simple depreciation (12%); × 0.96 × 3 triples the value.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A price rises by 30%, then falls by 20%. What is the overall percentage change?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 1.3 × 0.8 = 1.04, a 4% increase. Percentage changes multiply; they don't add.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A price rises by 20%, then the new price falls by 20%. What is the overall change?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, so it ends at 96% of the original: a 4% decrease.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: $2000 is invested at 5% per year compound interest. How much INTEREST is earned in 2 years?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 2000 × 1.05² = 2205, so the interest is 205. $200 is simple interest; $2205 is the total value, not the interest.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A car bought for $24 000 depreciates by 12% per year. What is it worth after 2 years?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 24 000 × 0.88² = 18 585.60. $18 240 takes 24% off in one go (simple depreciation).

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: $2880 is shared in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7. What is the largest share?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 15 parts, so 2880 ÷ 15 = 192 per part, and 7 × 192 = 1344. $411.43 is 2880 ÷ 7, dividing by a ratio number instead of the total.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Amir and Beth share money in the ratio 5 : 3. Amir gets $36 more than Beth. How much does Beth get?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 parts = $36, so 1 part = $18 and Beth gets 3 × 18 = $54 ($90 is Amir's share).

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Write the ratio 45 : 60 in its simplest form
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Divide both by the HCF, 15: 3 : 4. 9 : 12 and 15 : 20 are equivalent but not simplest; 4 : 3 is the wrong way round.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Write 2.5 × 10³ : 1.5 × 10⁶ in the form 1 : n
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Divide both parts by 2.5 × 10³: 1.5 × 10⁶ ÷ 2.5 × 10³ = 600.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5. What is a : b : c?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Make the b parts equal: 2 : 3 = 8 : 12 and 4 : 5 = 12 : 15, so a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: For the children at a show, girls : boys = 2 : 7. What fraction of the children are girls?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 2 + 7 = 9 parts, of which 2 are girls, so 2/9. 2/7 compares girls to boys, not girls to all children.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y is directly proportional to x². y = 45 when x = 3. What is the value of k in y = kx²?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 45 = k × 3² = 9k, so k = 5. 15 comes from using x instead of x².

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y = 5x². What is y when x = 4?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 5 × 4² = 5 × 16 = 80. 400 squares the 5 as well: (5 × 4)².

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: F is inversely proportional to d². F = 20 when d = 3. Which formula is correct?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: F = k/d², so 20 = k/9 and k = 180. 60/d² uses d instead of d² when finding k.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y is directly proportional to x³. What happens to y when x is doubled?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: k(2x)³ = 8kx³ = 8y.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: y is inversely proportional to x². What happens to y when x is tripled?
F is inversely proportional to d². d is increased by 25%. What is the percentage change in F?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: F is multiplied by 1/1.25² = 0.64, which is a 36% decrease.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Which graph shows that y is directly proportional to x?
options: A straight line crossing the y-axis above the origin
A curve through the origin that gets steeper
A curve that never meets either axis
A straight line through the origin
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: y = kx is a straight line through (0, 0). A line with a y-intercept (y = kx + c) is linear but not proportional. The steepening curve is y ∝ x² and the curve that never meets the axes is y ∝ 1/x.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: 'T is inversely proportional to the square root of L' means…
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Inversely proportional to √L: T = k ÷ √L.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: T = 48/√L. What is T when L = 36?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: √36 = 6, and 48 ÷ 6 = 8. 1.33 is 48 ÷ 36, which forgets the square root.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: £1 = €1.16. What is €348 in pounds?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Euros to pounds: divide by 1.16. 348 ÷ 1.16 = 300. Multiplying gives £403.68, the wrong direction.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: 3/5 of the people in a hall are children. There are 72 children. How many people are in the hall?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 3/5 = 72, so 1/5 = 24 and 5/5 = 120. 43.2 is 3/5 of 72, which works the wrong way.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A price falls from $552 to $480. What is the percentage decrease, to 3 significant figures?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Change 72 ÷ ORIGINAL 552 × 100 = 13.0%. 15% divides by the new price.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: A trader buys goods for $180 and sells them for $207. What is the percentage profit?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Profit 27 ÷ cost 180 × 100 = 15%.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: x is increased by 8% to give 27 000. Which calculation finds x?
$50 000 is invested at 3% per year compound interest. What is it worth after 2 years?
Dividing by 14/9 is the same as multiplying by…
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its reciprocal, because 14/9 × 9/14 = 1.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Write 36 as a fraction of 60, in its simplest form
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: 36/60: divide top and bottom by 12 to get 3/5. 36/60 is right but not simplest.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Which of these does NOT show y directly proportional to x?
02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.explain: Proportional means y = kx with no added constant. y = 2x + 3 does not double when x doubles.

02-fractions-percentages-ratio-proportio.q: Raj earns $20 000 and gets a 10% rise. Sam earns $17 600. What percentage rise must Sam get to earn the same as Raj?

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 7.2968 to 2 decimal places
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The third decimal is 6, so 7.29 rounds up to 7.30. Keep the trailing zero: it shows the accuracy is 2 dp.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 0.004076 to 2 significant figures
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The first significant figure is the 4. Keep 4 and 0; the next digit is 7, so round up to 0.0041.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 38 472 to 3 significant figures
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Keep 3, 8, 4; the next digit is 7, so round up to 385, then fill with zeros to keep the size: 38 500.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: How many significant figures does 0.04070 have?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Count from the first non-zero digit: 4, 0, 7, 0. The zero between 4 and 7 counts, and the final zero shows the accuracy.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Round 0.0060749 to 2 decimal places
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The second decimal place is 0 and the next digit is 6, so round up to 0.01. 0.0061 is 2 SIGNIFICANT figures, not 2 dp.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Estimate (48.7 × 3.12) ÷ 0.487 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: (50 × 3) ÷ 0.5 = 150 ÷ 0.5 = 300. Dividing by 0.5 DOUBLES. The exact value is 312.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A length is 6.4 cm correct to 1 decimal place. What is its upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Half of 0.1 is 0.05, so the bounds are 6.35 and 6.45. The upper bound is written 6.45, not 6.49.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A length l is 7.4 cm correct to 1 decimal place. Which is the error interval?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The lower bound 7.35 is included (it rounds up to 7.4) and the upper bound 7.45 is not (it would round to 7.5).

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: 3400 g is correct to 2 significant figures. What is the lower bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The second significant figure is in the hundreds, so it was rounded to the nearest 100. Half of 100 is 50: 3400 − 50 = 3350.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A mass is 70 kg to the nearest 5 kg. What are its bounds?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Half of 5 is 2.5, so 70 ± 2.5.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The distance from A to B is 110 km correct to 2 significant figures. What is the upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 2 sf, 110 is rounded to the nearest 10. Half of 10 is 5, so the upper bound is 115.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: There are 1300 sheets correct to the nearest 100. What is the lower bound?
a = 8.3 and b = 5.6, both to 1 dp. What is the upper bound of a × b?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: For a product, the maximum is UB × UB: 8.35 × 5.65 = 47.1775.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: a = 12.4 and b = 5.7, both to 1 dp. What is the upper bound of a − b?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Largest a minus SMALLEST b: 12.45 − 5.65 = 6.8. UB − UB gives 6.7, which is not the maximum.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: a = 12.4 and b = 5.7, both to 1 dp. What is the lower bound of a − b?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Smallest a minus LARGEST b: 12.35 − 5.75 = 6.6.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: e = 6.47 and f = 2.83, both to 2 dp. What is the upper bound of e − f?
Which gives the upper bound of a speed, where speed = distance ÷ time?
options: UB of distance ÷ UB of time
LB of distance ÷ LB of time
UB of distance ÷ LB of time
LB of distance ÷ UB of time
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: A fraction is largest with the biggest top and the smallest bottom. LB ÷ UB gives the LOWER bound.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A runner covers 200 m (nearest 5 m) in 24.6 s (nearest 0.1 s). What is the upper bound of the speed, to 3 sf?
1300 sheets (nearest 100) make a pile 160 mm high (nearest 10 mm). Which calculation gives the UPPER bound of the thickness of one sheet?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Thickness = height ÷ number. For the maximum: largest height ÷ smallest number = 165 ÷ 1250 = 0.132 mm.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: y = (a + b)/c with a = 5.3, b = 2.1 and c = 1.8, all to 1 dp. Which gives the upper bound of y?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Make the top as big as possible and the bottom as small as possible.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: y = 3a/(b − c). For the LARGEST y, which bounds of b and c should you use?
options: Lower bound of b and upper bound of c
Upper bound of b and lower bound of c
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To make y big, the denominator b − c must be SMALL: small b minus big c.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: y = 3a/(b − c) with a = 42, b = 31, c = 17, each to 2 sf. What is the lower bound of y, to 2 sf?
A rectangle is 20 cm by 11 cm, each to the nearest cm. What is the smallest possible area as a percentage of the largest, to 3 sf?
The side of a cube is 6.2 cm to 1 dp. What is the upper bound of its volume?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Use the upper bound of the side, 6.25, and cube it: 244.14… cm³.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A circle has area 50 cm² to the nearest cm². What is the lower bound of its radius, to 3 sf?
P = 23.7 × 8.46 (23.7 to 1 dp, 8.46 to 2 dp). The bounds of P are 199.96… and 201.04… To what accuracy can P be given?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 3 sf the bounds give 200 and 201, which disagree. To 2 sf both give 200, so P = 200 to 2 sf.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: z = x/y with bounds 13.478 (upper) and 13.423 (lower). What is z to a suitable degree of accuracy?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 3 sf the bounds round to 13.5 and 13.4, which disagree. To 2 sf both round to 13.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: An angle is 38° correct to 2 significant figures. What is its lower bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: To 2 sf, 38 is rounded to the nearest 1. Half of 1 is 0.5, so the lower bound is 37.5°.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The volume of a sphere of radius 2.35 cm is 54.36… cm³. What goes wrong if you round the radius to 2.4 first?
options: You get about 57.9 cm³, which is too big
Nothing: the answer still rounds to 54.4
You get about 54.9 cm³, which is slightly too big
You get about 52.0 cm³, which is too small
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 4/3 × π × 2.4³ = 57.9. Cubing magnifies the rounding error, so keep full values and round once at the end.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: 100 eggs are packed in boxes of 12. How many boxes are needed to hold all of them?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 100 ÷ 12 = 8.33… Eight boxes hold only 96 eggs, so round UP to 9 boxes.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A length is 5.8 cm correct to 2 significant figures. What is the upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 2 sf for 5.8 means to 1 dp. Half of 0.1 is 0.05, so the upper bound is 5.85.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The time taken for a journey is 150 km (2 sf) ÷ 60 km/h (nearest 5 km/h). Which gives the LOWER bound of the time?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Time = distance ÷ speed. The minimum is the smallest distance ÷ the largest speed = 145 ÷ 62.5 = 2.32 h.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Mass 440 g (nearest 10 g), volume 52 cm³ (nearest cm³). What is the upper bound of the density, to 3 sf?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 445 ÷ 51.5 = 8.640… → 8.64. Density is a division, so use UB mass ÷ LB volume.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A hypotenuse is 12 cm (nearest cm) and an angle is 40° (nearest degree). What is the upper bound of the opposite side, 12 sin 40°?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: sin increases between 0° and 90°, so the largest value uses the largest angle and the largest hypotenuse: 12.5 × sin 40.5° = 8.12 cm.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: Which is the correct way to give a final answer of 28 688.075… dollars?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Money is given to 2 dp (the nearest cent). The third decimal is 5, so round up to .08.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: The perimeter of a rectangle 8.3 cm by 5.6 cm (each to 1 dp) has what upper bound?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: 2 × (8.35 + 5.65) = 2 × 14 = 28. For a sum, use both upper bounds.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: x = 7.3 and y = 2.1, both to 1 dp. Which gives the LOWER bound of x ÷ y?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: For the smallest quotient, divide the smallest top by the largest bottom.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: A value is 2.4 to 1 dp. Why is 2.45 used as its upper bound, even though 2.45 rounds to 2.5?
options: Because 2.45 is closer to 2.4 than to 2.5
Because upper bounds are always rounded down
It isn't: the upper bound is 2.449
The value can be anything up to, but not including, 2.45
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: The true value can get as close to 2.45 as you like, so 2.45 is the boundary: 2.35 ≤ x < 2.45.

03-accuracy-and-bounds.q: With no instruction about accuracy, how should a non-exact decimal answer normally be given?
03-accuracy-and-bounds.explain: Edexcel expects 3 sf unless told otherwise (angles to 1 dp). Write the longer value first, then the rounded one.

04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: (3x − 2)(3x − 2) = 9x² − 6x − 6x + 4. Squaring each term misses the two middle terms.
(x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − x − 6; × (x + 4) gives x³ + 4x² − x² − 4x − 6x − 24 = x³ + 3x² − 10x − 24. The constant is 2 × −3 × 4 = −24.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: When (x + 5)(x − 3)(x + 3) is expanded, what is the constant term?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: The constant comes only from 5 × (−3) × 3 = −45.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: How many terms are there after multiplying a simplified quadratic (3 terms) by a bracket with 2 terms, before collecting?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 3 × 2 = 6 terms. Expanding all three brackets at once gives 8 terms. The 2018 scheme required the correct number of terms to be present.
HCF of 15 and 25 is 5, and the lowest powers are a² and b. The other answers still have a common factor left in the bracket.
HCF(24, 36) = 12; lowest powers a² and b². What is left is 2a − 3b².
The two numbers must multiply to −30 and add to +1: 6 and −5. (x − 6)(x + 5) gives −x.
Multiply to −40, add to −3: −8 and +5.
ac = −72; 9 and −8 multiply to −72 and add to 1. So 6x² + 9x − 8x − 12 = 3x(2x + 3) − 4(2x + 3).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: In the ac method for 6x² + x − 12, which two numbers do you look for?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Multiply a × c = 6 × −12 = −72, and the sum must be b = 1.
Difference of two squares: (5x)² − (6y)² = (5x − 6y)(5x + 6y).
Take out the common factor 2 first, then factorise the difference of squares: x² − 25 = (x − 5)(x + 5). 2(x² − 25) is not completely factorised.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Which of these can NOT be factorised using real numbers?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: x² + 9 is a SUM of squares. x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), 9 − x² = (3 − x)(3 + x), and x² − 9x = x(x − 9).
3x(x − 2) / ((x − 2)(x + 2)). Cancel the common FACTOR (x − 2).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: A student writes (x + 3)/(x + 5) = 3/5. What is wrong?
options: x is a term, not a factor, so it cannot be cancelled
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: You can only cancel factors. Test x = 1: 4/6 = 2/3, which is not 3/5.
[2(x − 1) + 5(x + 3)] / ((x + 3)(x − 1)) = (2x − 2 + 5x + 15)/… = (7x + 13)/((x + 3)(x − 1)). You cannot add the tops and bottoms separately.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: What is the simplest common denominator for 1/(9x² − 25) − 1/(6x + 10)?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 9x² − 25 = (3x − 5)(3x + 5) and 6x + 10 = 2(3x + 5). The LCM uses each factor once: 2(3x − 5)(3x + 5).
Common denominator 2(2x − 3)(2x + 3). Numerator 2 − (2x − 3) = 5 − 2x. The minus sign must go through the whole bracket.
Flip and multiply, then factorise: (x − 4)(x + 4)/[3(x + 4)] × 6x/[(x − 4)(x + 1)] = 2x/(x + 1).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make p the subject of N = pq − rs
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Add rs to both sides: pq = N + rs, then divide by q. Write p = at the start. The 2018 scheme only gave the A1 if the answer was seen with the subject and an equals sign.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make r the subject of V = πr²h/3
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 3V = πr²h, so r² = 3V/(πh) and r = √(3V/(πh)). Stopping at r² does not make r the subject.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make L the subject of T = 2π√(L/g)
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: T/(2π) = √(L/g), square: T²/(4π²) = L/g, then multiply by g.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make v the subject of E = ½mv² + h, where v is positive
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: E − h = ½mv², so v² = 2(E − h)/m, then take the positive square root.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make q the subject of p = (2q + 1)/(q − 3)
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: pq − 3p = 2q + 1 → pq − 2q = 1 + 3p → q(p − 2) = 1 + 3p. The first wrong answer still has q on both sides.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: When the subject appears in two terms, which step MUST you use?
options: Divide both sides by the subject
Cancel the subject from both sides
Factorise the subject out of the terms that contain it
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Collect the subject terms on one side, then factorise, e.g. q(p − 2) = 1 + 3p, so you can divide by the bracket.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make a the subject of 2a − 7 = (5 + a)/k

04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: Collect the g terms: 5g − 4eg = 3 − 2e, then factorise: g(5 − 4e) = 3 − 2e.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Make y the subject of x = √((y + 2)/(y − 1))
Which expression represents any odd number, where n is an integer?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: 2n is always even, so 2n + 1 is always odd. n + 1 and n² can be either odd or even.
4n² + 12n + 9 − (4n² + 4n + 1) = 8n + 8 = 8(n + 1), a multiple of 8.
(4n² + 12n + 9) − (4n² − 12n + 9) = 24n = 12 × 2n, so it is always a multiple of 12.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Why is 'it works for n = 1, 2 and 3' not a proof?
options: Examples only check some cases; a proof must work for every n
Three examples are not enough, but ten would be
It is a proof if the examples are chosen at random
It is a proof if n = 0 is also checked
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: However many examples you try, you have not covered every integer. Algebra with a general n does.

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: The sum of three consecutive integers n, n + 1 and n + 2 is always…
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), a multiple of 3. It can be odd or even (e.g. 6 and 9).

04-algebraic-manipulation.q: Which is an identity (true for ALL values of x)?
04-algebraic-manipulation.explain: An identity holds for every x. x² = 4 and 2x + 1 = 7 are equations; (x + 1)² = x² + 1 is false for most x.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve 3(x − 4) = 2x + 5
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Expand: 3x − 12 = 2x + 5. Subtract 2x and add 12: x = 17. The answer 9 comes from forgetting to multiply the −4 by 3.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve (x + 5)/3 = 4
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Multiply both sides by 3: x + 5 = 12, so x = 7. Multiply the whole of the left side, not just the x.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve the inequality 7 − 2x > 13
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: −2x > 6. Dividing by −2 reverses the sign, so x < −3. The answer x > −3 forgets to flip it.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Which integers satisfy −3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 7?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Subtract 1 from all three parts: −4 < 2x ≤ 6. Halve: −2 < x ≤ 3. −2 is not included (strict <) but 3 is (≤).

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: A number line has an open circle at 2, a filled circle at 5 and the part between them shaded. Which inequality does it show?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: An open circle means the value is not included (<). A filled circle means it is included (≤). So 2 < x ≤ 5.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 11 and x − y = 1
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Add the equations to eliminate y: 3x = 12, so x = 4. Then 4 − y = 1, so y = 3. Check: 2(4) + 3 = 11.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: To eliminate y from 3x + 2y = 12 and 5x − 2y = 4, what should you do?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: The y-coefficients are +2 and −2, which have different signs, so adding makes them cancel: 8x = 16.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve 4x + 3y = 18 and 2x + 3y = 12
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Same signs, so subtract: 2x = 6, x = 3. Then 6 + 3y = 12, so y = 2. Always check the pair in both equations.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Two straight lines cross at the point (2, −1). What is the solution of their simultaneous equations?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: The crossing point lies on both lines, so its coordinates satisfy both equations: x = 2, y = −1.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve x² + 3x − 10 = 0
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: (x + 5)(x − 2) = 0, so x = −5 or x = 2. The signs flip when you set each bracket to zero.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve x² = 6x
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x² − 6x = 0, so x(x − 6) = 0, giving x = 0 or x = 6. Dividing both sides by x loses the solution x = 0.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve x² − 49 = 0
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x² = 49, so x = ±7. It is a difference of two squares: (x − 7)(x + 7) = 0. Forgetting the negative root loses a mark.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Factorise 2x² + 7x + 3
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: ac = 6. The numbers 6 and 1 multiply to 6 and add to 7: 2x² + 6x + x + 3 = 2x(x + 3) + 1(x + 3) = (2x + 1)(x + 3). (2x + 3)(x + 1) expands to 2x² + 5x + 3.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve 3x² − 5x − 2 = 0
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: (3x + 1)(x − 2) = 0, so x = −1/3 or x = 2. Divide by the 3 in the bracket: 3x + 1 = 0 gives x = −1/3.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Which is the correct substitution into the quadratic formula for 2x² − 3x − 4 = 0?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: a = 2, b = −3, c = −4. −b = 3. b² − 4ac = 9 − 4(2)(−4) = 9 + 32. 2a = 4. Watch the signs of b and c.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve x² + 4x − 7 = 0, giving your answers to 3 significant figures.
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x = (−4 ± √(16 + 28)) ÷ 2 = (−4 ± √44) ÷ 2 = −2 ± √11, which is 1.3166… or −5.3166…. A quadratic like this has two answers.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: What is the value of b² − 4ac for 3x² + 2x + 5 = 0?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: b² − 4ac = 2² − 4 × 3 × 5 = 4 − 60 = −56. It is negative, so the equation has no real solutions.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: For a quadratic equation, b² − 4ac is negative. What does that tell you?
options: One positive and one negative solution
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: You cannot square-root a negative number, so the formula gives no real answers. The graph does not cross the x-axis.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Write x² + 10x + 7 in the form (x + p)² + q
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Half of 10 is 5: (x + 5)² − 25 + 7 = (x + 5)² − 18. The 25 must be subtracted, not added.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: What are the coordinates of the turning point of y = (x − 3)² + 4?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: The bracket is zero when x = 3, and then y = 4. The minimum point is (3, 4). The x-coordinate has the opposite sign to the number in the bracket.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Write 2x² + 8x + 1 in the form a(x + b)² + c
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: 2(x² + 4x) + 1 = 2[(x + 2)² − 4] + 1 = 2(x + 2)² − 8 + 1 = 2(x + 2)² − 7. The −4 inside the bracket gets multiplied by 2.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve (x − 2)² = 5
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Square-root both sides, remembering ±: x − 2 = ±√5, so x = 2 ± √5.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: What is the minimum value of x² − 6x + 11?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x² − 6x + 11 = (x − 3)² + 2. A square is never negative, so the smallest value is 2, when x = 3.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: A rectangle is (x + 2) cm long and x cm wide. Its area is 35 cm². Which equation must x satisfy?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x(x + 2) = 35 gives x² + 2x = 35, so x² + 2x − 35 = 0. It factorises as (x + 7)(x − 5), so x = 5.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: A quadratic from a context gives x = 6 or x = −9, where x is a length in cm. What should you write?
options: Give x = 6 and reject x = −9, because a length cannot be negative
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: The algebra gives both roots, but a length must be positive. Reject −9 and say why, then use x = 6.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Substituting y = x + 2 into x² + y² = 20 gives which equation?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x² + (x + 2)² = 20 gives x² + x² + 4x + 4 = 20, so 2x² + 4x − 16 = 0. (x + 2)² has a middle term, 4x.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve the simultaneous equations y = x + 2 and x² + y² = 20
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: 2x² + 4x − 16 = 0, so x² + 2x − 8 = 0, so (x + 4)(x − 2) = 0. x = 2 gives y = 4, and x = −4 gives y = −2. Find each y from the linear equation.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Where does the line y = 2x − 1 meet the curve y = x² − 4?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x² − 4 = 2x − 1 gives x² − 2x − 3 = 0, so (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0. x = 3 gives y = 5, and x = −1 gives y = −3.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve x² < 25
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: The critical values are ±5. x² − 25 < 0 is below the axis, which is between the roots: −5 < x < 5. x = −10 satisfies x < 5 but not x² < 25.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve x² − 5x + 4 > 0
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: (x − 1)(x − 4) = 0 gives critical values 1 and 4. Greater than 0 means above the axis, which is the two tails: x < 1 or x > 4.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve (x − 2)(x + 6) ≤ 0
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: The critical values are 2 and −6. A U-shaped graph is at or below the axis between them: −6 ≤ x ≤ 2.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve 2x² ≥ 50
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: x² ≥ 25. The critical values are ±5, and 'greater than or equal to' gives the tails: x ≤ −5 or x ≥ 5.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: How many integers satisfy x² ≤ 10?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: −√10 ≤ x ≤ √10, about −3.16 to 3.16. The integers are −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and 3: seven of them. Don't forget the negatives and 0.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Which point lies in the region y ≥ 1, x + y ≤ 5 and y ≤ 2x?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: (2, 2): 2 ≥ 1, 2 + 2 = 4 ≤ 5 and 2 ≤ 4, so all three are true. (0, 3) fails y ≤ 2x, (4, 3) fails x + y ≤ 5, and (3, 0) fails y ≥ 1.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Which side of the line 3x + 2y = 12 is the region 3x + 2y < 12?
options: The side that does not contain the origin
The side that contains the origin
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Test (0, 0): 0 < 12 is true, so the region is on the same side as the origin.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: At which vertex do the boundary lines y = 2 and x + y = 8 meet?
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Put y = 2 into x + y = 8: x = 6. The vertex is (6, 2), and it satisfies both equations.
× 6: 3(3x − 1) − 2(x + 1) = 6, so 9x − 3 − 2x − 2 = 6, so 7x = 11 and x = 11/7. Writing −2x + 2 instead of −2x − 2 gives the wrong answer 1.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: Solve −4x ≤ 20
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: Divide by −4 and reverse the sign: x ≥ −5. Check with x = 0: 0 ≤ 20 is true, and 0 is in x ≥ −5.

05-equations-and-inequalities.q: The angles of a triangle are x°, (2x + 10)° and (3x − 40)°. Find x.
Why does the line y = 3x − 10 not meet the circle x² + y² = 8? (Substituting gives 5x² − 30x + 46 = 0.)
05-equations-and-inequalities.explain: (−30)² − 4 × 5 × 46 = 900 − 920 = −20 < 0, so there are no real solutions and no intersection. 'It does not factorise' is not a reason: many quadratics with real roots do not factorise.

06-sequences.q: What is the next term of 7, 11, 15, 19, …?
06-sequences.explain: The difference is +4 each time, so 19 + 4 = 23.

06-sequences.q: What is the term-to-term rule for 3, 6, 12, 24, …?
06-sequences.explain: The differences (3, 6, 12) are not constant, but each term is double the one before, so the rule is multiply by 2.

06-sequences.q: What is the nth term of 4, 9, 14, 19, …?
06-sequences.explain: The difference is 5, so 5n. 5n gives 5, 10, 15, … and each term is 1 less, so 5n − 1. Check: n = 1 gives 4.

06-sequences.q: What is the nth term of 2, 9, 16, 23, …? (SAM 2H)
06-sequences.explain: The difference is 7. 7n gives 7, 14, 21, …, which is 5 too big, so 7n − 5. The scheme gave only M1 for 7n + k, and A1 needs the −5.

06-sequences.q: What is the nth term of 30, 26, 22, 18, …?
06-sequences.explain: The difference is −4, so −4n. −4n gives −4, −8, …, and 34 must be added to get 30, so 34 − 4n. 30 − 4n gives 26 as the first term.

06-sequences.q: The nth term of a sequence is 6n − 4. What is the 10th term?
What are the first three terms of the sequence with nth term n² + 2?
06-sequences.explain: n = 1: 1 + 2 = 3. n = 2: 4 + 2 = 6. n = 3: 9 + 2 = 11. The differences are 3, 5, … so it is not arithmetic.

06-sequences.q: Is 150 a term of the sequence with nth term 4n + 2?
options: No, 150 is not a multiple of 4
06-sequences.explain: 4n + 2 = 150 gives 4n = 148, so n = 37, a whole number. So 150 is the 37th term.

06-sequences.q: Is 100 a term of the sequence with nth term 3n − 1?
options: No, because n = 33.67, which is not a whole number
06-sequences.explain: 3n − 1 = 100 gives n = 101 ÷ 3 = 33.67 (2 d.p.), which is not an integer, so 100 is not a term. The reason must come from solving for n.

06-sequences.q: What is the first term of the sequence 5n + 3 that is greater than 100?
06-sequences.explain: 5n + 3 > 100 gives n > 19.4, so n = 20 and the term is 5 × 20 + 3 = 103. The 19th term, 98, is still below 100.

06-sequences.q: What is the 15th term of the arithmetic sequence 2, 5, 8, …?
06-sequences.explain: a + (n − 1)d = 2 + 14 × 3 = 44. Using a + nd gives 47, one step too many.

06-sequences.q: An arithmetic sequence has first term 10 and common difference −3. What is its 8th term?
06-sequences.explain: 10 + 7 × (−3) = 10 − 21 = −11. There are 7 steps from the 1st term to the 8th.

06-sequences.q: The 2nd term of an arithmetic sequence is 11 and the 6th term is 27. Find a and d.
06-sequences.explain: a + d = 11 and a + 5d = 27. Subtract: 4d = 16, so d = 4, and then a = 7. From term 2 to term 6 is 4 steps, not 5.

06-sequences.q: The 4th term of an arithmetic series is 17 and the 10th term is 35. What is the common difference? (SAM 1H)
06-sequences.explain: From the 4th term to the 10th is 6 steps, and the value rises by 35 − 17 = 18. So d = 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

06-sequences.q: Which of these is given on the 4MA1 Higher formula sheet?
06-sequences.explain: The formula sheet gives the sum of an arithmetic series, Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d]. The nth term a + (n − 1)d must be memorised.

06-sequences.q: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of 3 + 7 + 11 + 15 + …
06-sequences.explain: S₂₀ = 20/2 [2 × 3 + 19 × 4] = 10 × 82 = 820. 79 is the 20th term, not the sum.

06-sequences.q: How many terms are there in 5 + 8 + 11 + … + 62?
06-sequences.explain: (62 − 5) ÷ 3 + 1 = 19 + 1 = 20. Dividing the gap by d counts the steps; add 1 to count the terms.

06-sequences.q: Find the sum 5 + 8 + 11 + … + 62
How many multiples of 4 are there from 100 to 200 inclusive?
For the series 2 + 6 + 10 + …, what does Sₙ simplify to?
How many terms of 2 + 6 + 10 + … are needed for a sum of 800?
06-sequences.explain: Sₙ = 2n² = 800, so n² = 400 and n = 20. n must be a positive whole number.

06-sequences.q: Solving Sₙ = 390 gives n = 12 or n = −15.5. What is the answer?
options: n = 12, because n must be a positive whole number
06-sequences.explain: n counts terms, so it must be a positive integer. Reject −15.5 and give the reason.

06-sequences.q: Which of these is a series, rather than a sequence?
06-sequences.explain: A series is the terms added together. 4, 7, 10, 13 is a sequence, a list.

06-sequences.q: Which of these is NOT an arithmetic sequence?
06-sequences.explain: 1, 4, 9, 16 has differences 3, 5, 7, which are not constant. The others have constant differences 0, −3 and 0.5.

06-sequences.q: What is the common difference of 7, 4.5, 2, …?
06-sequences.explain: 4.5 − 7 = −2.5. The sequence is decreasing, so d is negative.

06-sequences.q: Why is the coefficient of n in the nth term 3n + 2 equal to 3?
options: Because the sequence goes up by 3 each time
06-sequences.explain: When n increases by 1, 3n increases by 3 and the +2 stays the same, so consecutive terms differ by 3.

06-sequences.q: The nth term of a sequence is 20 − 3n. Which is the first negative term?
06-sequences.explain: 20 − 3n < 0 gives n > 6.67, so n = 7 (20 − 21 = −1). The 6th term is 2, which is still positive.

06-sequences.q: The 5th term of an arithmetic series is 14 and the sum of the first 10 terms is 155. Find a and d.
06-sequences.explain: a + 4d = 14 and 5(2a + 9d) = 155, so 2a + 9d = 31. Doubling the first gives 2a + 8d = 28. Subtract: d = 3, and a = 2.

06-sequences.q: An arithmetic series has 2a + 29d = 0. What is the sum of its first 30 terms?
options: It cannot be found without a and d
06-sequences.explain: S₃₀ = 30/2 [2a + 29d] = 15 × 0 = 0. This was the key step in 2018 2H Q23: you never need a and d separately.

06-sequences.q: A theatre has 20 seats in row 1, and each row has 2 more seats than the row in front. How many seats are in row 15?
06-sequences.explain: 20 + 14 × 2 = 48. There are 14 steps from row 1 to row 15.

06-sequences.q: Sam saves $10 in week 1, and $5 more each week than the week before. How much has he saved in total after 12 weeks?
06-sequences.explain: S₁₂ = 12/2 [20 + 11 × 5] = 6 × 75 = $450. $65 is what he saves in week 12 alone.

06-sequences.q: Patterns use 4, 7, 10, … matchsticks. How many matchsticks are in pattern 50?
06-sequences.explain: The nth term is 3n + 1, so pattern 50 uses 3 × 50 + 1 = 151.

06-sequences.q: A sequence has term-to-term rule 'add 5', and its 3rd term is 17. What is its first term?
06-sequences.explain: Work backwards two steps: 17 − 5 − 5 = 7.

06-sequences.q: An arithmetic sequence has 3rd term 8 and 7th term 20. What is its 20th term?
What is the sum of the first 10 even numbers, 2 + 4 + … + 20?
What is the sum of the first n odd numbers, 1 + 3 + 5 + …?
06-sequences.explain: a = 1, d = 2: Sₙ = n/2 [2 + 2(n − 1)] = n/2 × 2n = n². 2n − 1 is the nth odd number itself, not the sum.

06-sequences.q: Row n of a number pattern contains (n + 1)². Which row contains 144?
What is the 25th term of the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16, …?
06-sequences.explain: These are the square numbers, nth term n², so the 25th term is 25² = 625.

06-sequences.q: The sum of the first n terms of a series is Sₙ = 3n² + 2n. What is the first term?
06-sequences.explain: The sum of the first 1 term is the first term itself: S₁ = 3 + 2 = 5.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: f(x) = 2x² − 3. Find f(−2).
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: f(−2) = 2 × (−2)² − 3 = 2 × 4 − 3 = 5. Square first, with the negative in brackets.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: f(x) = 3x + 1. Solve f(x) = 13.
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: 3x + 1 = 13, so 3x = 12 and x = 4. 40 is f(13), not the solution of f(x) = 13.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: What does fg(x) mean?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: fg(x) = f(g(x)). The function next to the x acts first, so g is applied first and then f.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = x². Find fg(2).
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: g(2) = 4, then f(4) = 7. 25 is gf(2), which does the functions in the wrong order.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x + 4. Find gf(x).
f(x) = 5x − 2. Find f⁻¹(x).
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: y = 5x − 2, so y + 2 = 5x and x = (y + 2)/5. So f⁻¹(x) = (x + 2)/5. The inverse is not the reciprocal.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: f(x) = (x + 4)/3. Find f⁻¹(x).
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: y = (x + 4)/3, so 3y = x + 4 and x = 3y − 4. So f⁻¹(x) = 3x − 4. Undo the operations in reverse order.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Which value of x must be excluded from any domain of f(x) = 4/(x + 3)?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: The denominator is zero when x + 3 = 0, i.e. x = −3, and you cannot divide by zero.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: g(x) = √(x − 2). Which values of x cannot be in any domain of g?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: You need x − 2 ≥ 0, so x ≥ 2. The values that fail are x < 2. x = 2 is fine, because √0 = 0.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: What is the range of f(x) = x² + 5?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: x² is never negative and equals 0 when x = 0, so the smallest output is 5, and 5 itself is included: f(x) ≥ 5.
g(3) = √16 = 4, the positive root only. f(4) = 7/4 = 1.75. The scheme gave the A1 only for 1.75 'and no other solution'.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: What is the gradient of the line through (1, 3) and (4, 12)?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Change in y ÷ change in x = (12 − 3) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3. 1/3 comes from dividing the wrong way round.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Find the gradient and y-intercept of 2y = 6x − 8
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Divide by 2 first: y = 3x − 4. The gradient is 3 and the line crosses the y-axis at (0, −4).

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Find the midpoint of (−2, 7) and (6, 1)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: ((−2 + 6)/2, (7 + 1)/2) = (2, 4). Take the mean of the x-coordinates and the mean of the y-coordinates.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Find the length of the line segment from (1, 2) to (7, 10)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10. It is Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical steps.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient −2 that passes through (3, 5)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: 5 = −2(3) + c, so c = 11: y = −2x + 11. The point (3, 5) is not the y-intercept, so c is not 5.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: A line has gradient 2/3. What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to it?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1: flip the fraction and change the sign, giving −3/2.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Find the equation of the line parallel to y = 4 − 2x that passes through (3, 7)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Parallel lines have the same gradient, −2. 7 = −2(3) + c, so c = 13: y = −2x + 13.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Which line is perpendicular to y = 3x + 5?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: 6y + 2x = 1 gives y = 1/6 − x/3, with gradient −1/3, and 3 × (−1/3) = −1. 3y = x + 2 has gradient 1/3, so it has the flip without the sign change.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Which is an equation of the line through (−3, 5) and (1, 2)? (SAM 1H)
What does the graph of y = −x² + 4 look like?
options: A U-shape with a minimum at (0, 4)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: A negative x² term makes a ∩-shape. When x = 0, y = 4, so the maximum is at (0, 4).

07-functions-and-graphs.q: What does the graph of y = 3/x look like?
options: A U-shaped curve through the origin
Two separate branches, in the 1st and 3rd quadrants
A straight line through the origin
Two branches, in the 2nd and 4th quadrants
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: A reciprocal graph never touches the axes. With a positive k, x and y have the same sign, so the branches are in the 1st and 3rd quadrants.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Where does y = x³ − 4x cross the x-axis?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: x³ − 4x = x(x² − 4) = x(x − 2)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 0, 2 or −2. A cubic can cross the axis up to three times.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Solve sin x = 0.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°, and by symmetry the second solution is 180° − 30° = 150°.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Solve cos x = −0.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: cos⁻¹(−0.5) = 120°, and cos is symmetrical about 180°, so the second solution is 360° − 120° = 240°.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Solve tan x = 1 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: tan repeats every 180°, so the solutions are 45° and 45° + 180° = 225°.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: How often does the graph of y = tan x repeat?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: sin and cos repeat every 360°, but tan repeats every 180°. It is undefined at 90°, 270°, and so on.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: y = f(x) has a maximum at (3, 5). Where is the maximum of y = f(x + 3)?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: f(x + 3) is a translation 3 to the LEFT: (3 − 3, 5) = (0, 5). A change inside the bracket works the opposite way.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: y = f(x) has a maximum at (3, 5). Where is the maximum of y = f(3x)?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: f(3x) is a stretch parallel to the x-axis with scale factor 1/3, so x is divided by 3: (1, 5).

07-functions-and-graphs.q: y = f(x) has a minimum at (−2, −1). Where is the minimum of y = ½f(x)? (2018 1H)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: ½f(x) is outside the bracket, so it halves y: (−2, −0.5). The x-coordinate is unchanged.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: Describe the transformation that maps y = f(x) to y = f(x) − 4
options: Stretch parallel to the y-axis, scale factor −4
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Subtracting 4 outside the function lowers every y by 4: a translation by (0, −4). Name the transformation and give its vector.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: What does y = −f(x) do to the graph of y = f(x)?
options: Reflection in the line y = x
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Every y changes sign, so the graph flips over the x-axis. y = f(−x) would be the reflection in the y-axis.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: What is the maximum value of y = 2 sin(x − 90)° + 1?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: sin is at most 1, so y is at most 2 × 1 + 1 = 3. The −90 only shifts the graph sideways.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: The graph of y = x² is drawn. Which line should you draw to solve x² − x − 6 = 0?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: x² − x − 6 = 0 means x² = x + 6, so draw y = x + 6. The x-coordinates of the crossings (−2 and 3) are the solutions.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: The graph of y = x³ − 2x² − 3x + 4 is drawn. Which line solves x³ − 2x² − x + 1 = 0? (2018 2H)
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: (x³ − 2x² − 3x + 4) − (x³ − 2x² − x + 1) = −2x + 3. Where the curve meets y = −2x + 3, the new equation is true.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: When you solve an equation using two graphs, what are the solutions?
options: The y-coordinates of the crossing points
The points where the curve crosses the y-axis
The x-coordinates of the crossing points
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: At a crossing point both graphs have the same y for the same x, so the x-values make the two expressions equal.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: A tangent to a curve at (2, 5) passes through (4, 13). What is the gradient of the curve at x = 2?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: The gradient of the tangent is (13 − 5) ÷ (4 − 2) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4, and that is the gradient of the curve at that point.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 15 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Acceleration is the gradient of the speed–time graph: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 m/s². 75 is the area under the line, not the gradient.

07-functions-and-graphs.q: A cyclist travels at 12 m/s for 10 s, then decelerates uniformly to rest in 4 s. How far does she travel altogether?
07-functions-and-graphs.explain: Distance = area under the speed–time graph: 12 × 10 + ½ × 4 × 12 = 120 + 24 = 144 m. 168 m wrongly treats the slowing-down part as a rectangle.

08-differentiation.q: Differentiate y = x⁵
08-differentiation.explain: Bring the power down and reduce it by 1: 5x⁴.

08-differentiation.q: Differentiate y = 4x³
08-differentiation.explain: 3 × 4x² = 12x². Multiply by the power and reduce the power by 1.

08-differentiation.q: Find dy/dx for y = 6x² − 5x + 8
08-differentiation.explain: 6x² → 12x, −5x → −5, and the constant 8 → 0. So dy/dx = 12x − 5.

08-differentiation.q: Differentiate y = 7x
08-differentiation.explain: 7x = 7x¹, so 1 × 7x⁰ = 7. The line y = 7x has gradient 7 everywhere.

08-differentiation.q: Differentiate y = 9
08-differentiation.explain: y = 9 is a horizontal line, so its gradient is 0. A constant always differentiates to 0.

08-differentiation.q: Find dy/dx for y = 3/x
08-differentiation.explain: Rewrite as 3x⁻¹. Then −1 × 3x⁻² = −3x⁻², or −3/x². The power goes from −1 down to −2.

08-differentiation.q: Find dy/dx for y = 2/x²
08-differentiation.explain: 2x⁻² → −2 × 2x⁻³ = −4x⁻³. The power −2 goes down to −3, not up to −1.

08-differentiation.q: Find dy/dx for y = (x + 2)(x − 5)
08-differentiation.explain: Expand first: x² − 3x − 10. Then dy/dx = 2x − 3. Differentiating each bracket and multiplying (1 × 1) is wrong.

08-differentiation.q: Find dy/dx for y = (x³ + 6x)/x
08-differentiation.explain: Simplify first: x³/x + 6x/x = x² + 6. Then dy/dx = 2x.

08-differentiation.q: Find the gradient of y = x² − 3x at the point where x = 4
08-differentiation.explain: dy/dx = 2x − 3, and at x = 4 this is 8 − 3 = 5. 4 is the y-coordinate (16 − 12), not the gradient.

08-differentiation.q: Find the gradient of y = x³ at the point where x = −2
08-differentiation.explain: dy/dx = 3x² = 3 × (−2)² = 12. The square makes it positive: y = x³ is always going uphill.

08-differentiation.q: What condition gives the stationary points of a curve?
08-differentiation.explain: At a stationary point the curve is momentarily flat, so its gradient is zero.

08-differentiation.q: Find the stationary point of y = x² − 8x + 3
08-differentiation.explain: dy/dx = 2x − 8 = 0 gives x = 4. y = 16 − 32 + 3 = −13. Find y from the original equation.

08-differentiation.q: Find the stationary point of y = 8x² + 2/x (SAM 1H)
y = 12x − x³ has stationary points at x = 2 and x = −2. Which one is the maximum?
08-differentiation.explain: The −x³ term makes it a negative cubic: it falls, rises, then falls. So the right-hand point is the maximum. y = 24 − 8 = 16.

08-differentiation.q: A cubic with a positive x³ term has stationary points at x = −1 and x = 3. Where is the maximum?
options: You cannot tell without a graph
08-differentiation.explain: A positive cubic rises, turns down, then turns back up, so the left-hand (smaller x) stationary point is the maximum.

08-differentiation.q: Find the nature and position of the stationary point of y = 5 + 4x − x²
08-differentiation.explain: dy/dx = 4 − 2x = 0 gives x = 2, and y = 5 + 8 − 4 = 9. The −x² term makes a ∩-shape, so it is a maximum.

08-differentiation.q: For which values of x does y = x³ − 2x² − 15x + 5 have a negative gradient? (2018 2H)
08-differentiation.explain: 3x² − 4x − 15 < 0, which factorises as (3x + 5)(x − 3) < 0. Between the roots: −5/3 < x < 3. The scheme required the inequality signs.

08-differentiation.q: For which values of x is y = x² − 6x increasing?
08-differentiation.explain: dy/dx = 2x − 6 > 0 gives x > 3. To the right of the minimum at x = 3, the curve goes uphill.

08-differentiation.q: Find the point on y = x² + 2x where the gradient is 10
08-differentiation.explain: 2x + 2 = 10 gives x = 4, and y = 16 + 8 = 24. The gradient is 10, but the y-coordinate is not.

08-differentiation.q: At which values of x does y = x³ − 4x² + 5x + 4 have gradient 1?
A = 60x − 1.5x². Find the maximum value of A.
08-differentiation.explain: dA/dx = 60 − 3x = 0 gives x = 20. A = 1200 − 600 = 600. 20 is the value of x, not the maximum area.

08-differentiation.q: V = 28x² − 2x³. Which value of x gives the maximum V?
08-differentiation.explain: dV/dx = 56x − 6x² = 2x(28 − 3x) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 28/3. x = 0 gives zero volume, so the maximum is at x = 28/3.

08-differentiation.q: You have found that dA/dx = 0 when x = 30. What should you do next to find the maximum area?
options: Substitute x = 30 into the formula for A
Give x = 30 as the maximum area
08-differentiation.explain: x = 30 tells you where the maximum is. The maximum value is A at x = 30. Putting x = 30 into dA/dx just gives 0.

08-differentiation.q: s = t³ − 5t² − 8t + 3. Find the velocity v.
08-differentiation.explain: v = ds/dt: t³ → 3t², −5t² → −10t, −8t → −8, and the constant 3 → 0.

08-differentiation.q: A particle is 'instantaneously at rest'. Which condition do you use?
08-differentiation.explain: At rest means not moving, so the velocity is zero. s = 0 means the particle is at O.

08-differentiation.q: 3t² − 10t − 8 = 0 gives t = 4 or t = −2/3, with t ≥ 0. When is the particle at rest? (SAM 2H)
08-differentiation.explain: Time cannot be negative, so reject −2/3. The mark scheme said 'A1 t = 4 only'.

08-differentiation.q: v = 3t² − 10t − 8. Find the acceleration a.
08-differentiation.explain: a = dv/dt: 3t² → 6t, −10t → −10, and the constant −8 → 0.

08-differentiation.q: s = 24t² − t³. Find the velocity.
08-differentiation.explain: ds/dt = 48t − 3t². 48 − 6t is the acceleration, which comes from differentiating a second time.

08-differentiation.q: Which condition gives the maximum velocity of a particle?
08-differentiation.explain: Velocity is greatest where its graph is at a peak, and there its gradient, the acceleration, is zero.

08-differentiation.q: s = 24t² − t³, 0 ≤ t ≤ 20. Find the maximum velocity.
08-differentiation.explain: a = 48 − 6t = 0 gives t = 8. v = 48(8) − 3(64) = 384 − 192 = 192 m/s. 1024 is the displacement at t = 8, and 8 is the time.

08-differentiation.q: s = 2t³ − 21t² + 60t. What is the initial velocity?
08-differentiation.explain: v = 6t² − 42t + 60. 'Initially' means t = 0, so v = 60 m/s. The particle starts at O (s = 0) but is already moving.

08-differentiation.q: v = 3t² − 12t + 9. When is the particle at rest?
08-differentiation.explain: 3(t² − 4t + 3) = 3(t − 1)(t − 3) = 0, so t = 1 or t = 3. t = 2 is when the acceleration is zero.

08-differentiation.q: a = 6t − 12. What is the acceleration when t = 5?
A question says the particle 'returns to O'. Which condition do you use?
08-differentiation.explain: s is the displacement from O, so being back at O means s = 0.

08-differentiation.q: y = ax² + bx. Find dy/dx.
08-differentiation.explain: ax² → 2ax and bx → b. The letters a and b are constants and are treated like numbers.

08-differentiation.q: For an open box, V = 4x³ − 120x² + 900x and dV/dx = 0 gives x = 5 or x = 15. The card is 30 cm square. Which gives the maximum?
options: x = 5, because x = 15 leaves no base
08-differentiation.explain: At x = 15 the base is 30 − 2 × 15 = 0 cm wide, so V = 0, which is a minimum. The maximum is at x = 5: V = 5 × 20² = 2000 cm³.

08-differentiation.q: V is in cm³ and r is in cm. What are the units of dV/dr?
08-differentiation.explain: dV/dr is the rate of change of V with r: cm³ per cm, which is cm².

08-differentiation.q: y = x². What is the gradient of the curve at x = 3?
08-differentiation.explain: dy/dx = 2x, so at x = 3 the gradient is 6. 9 is the y-value.

08-differentiation.q: Differentiate y = 5x⁴ − 2x⁻¹
08-differentiation.explain: 5x⁴ → 20x³. −2x⁻¹ → (−1)(−2)x⁻² = +2x⁻². Two negatives make a positive.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Two angles lie on a straight line. One of them is 127°. What is the other?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 180 − 127 = 53°. 233° comes from using 360°, which is for angles at a point.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: PQ is parallel to RS. A straight line crossing both makes an angle of 74° with PQ. What is the alternate angle at RS?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Alternate angles are equal, so it is 74°. 106° is the co-interior angle (180 − 74), which is a different pair.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What is true of co-interior (allied) angles between parallel lines?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Co-interior angles (the C or U shape) add up to 180°. Alternate and corresponding angles are the pairs that are equal.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Which reason would an examiner accept for two angles in a Z shape between parallel lines?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The accepted wording is "alternate angles are equal". The letter shapes are memory aids only, and corresponding angles are the F shape.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: The two interior opposite angles of a triangle are 48° and 67°. What is the exterior angle at the third vertex?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles: 48 + 67 = 115°. 65° is the interior angle at that vertex.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40°. What is each base angle?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The base angles are equal and the three angles add up to 180°: (180 − 40) ÷ 2 = 70°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A quadrilateral has angles 95°, 110°, 70° and x°. What is x?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°: 360 − (95 + 110 + 70) = 360 − 275 = 85. 5 comes from using 180° as the total.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of an octagon?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: (n − 2) × 180 = 6 × 180 = 1080°. 1440° is 8 × 180, forgetting the − 2, and 360° is the sum of the exterior angles.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What is each exterior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Exterior angles add up to 360°, so each is 360 ÷ 12 = 30°. 150° is the interior angle (180 − 30).

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Exterior angle = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°, so interior = 180 − 60 = 120°. 720° is the total of all six, and 108° is a pentagon's angle.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. How many sides does it have?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: n = 360 ÷ exterior angle = 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 162°. How many sides does it have?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Go through the exterior angle: 180 − 162 = 18°, so n = 360 ÷ 18 = 20. Dividing 360 by the interior angle (2.2) is the classic error.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A hexagon has angles 100°, 130°, 125°, 140°, y° and y°. What is y?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Hexagon sum = (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°. 720 − 495 = 225, and there are two y's, so y = 112.5. 22.5 comes from using the pentagon total 540°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: The interior angle of a regular polygon with n sides is 140°. What is the interior angle of a regular polygon with 2n sides?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Exterior 40°, so n = 9 and 2n = 18. Exterior angle of the 18-gon = 360 ÷ 18 = 20°, so interior = 160°. Doubling the sides does not double or halve the angle.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: The bearing of B from A is 070°. What is the bearing of A from B?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: A back bearing differs by 180°: 070 + 180 = 250°. 110° is 180 − 70, which is not a bearing rule.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: The bearing of Q from P is 305°. What is the bearing of P from Q?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: 305 + 180 goes past 360, so subtract instead: 305 − 180 = 125°. (485 − 360 = 125 too.)

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Which of these is written correctly as a three-figure bearing?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Bearings are measured clockwise from north and written with three figures, so 45° is written 045°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What is the first step in constructing the bisector of angle ABC with ruler and compasses?
options: Measure the angle with a protractor and halve it
With the compass point on B, draw an arc crossing both arms BA and BC
Draw arcs of different radii from A and from C
Join B to the midpoint of AC
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The SAM 1H scheme's M1 was for a circular arc, centre B, crossing both lines. A protractor is not a construction, and B to the midpoint of AC only bisects the angle if AB = BC.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: To construct the perpendicular bisector of AB, the compasses must be opened to
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The arcs from A and B must cross, so the radius must be more than half of AB, and the same radius is used from both ends.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What does "congruent" mean?
options: Exactly the same shape and size
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Congruent shapes are identical in shape and size. The same shape at a different size is similar.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Which of these does NOT prove that two triangles are congruent?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Three equal angles fix the shape but not the size, so AAA only proves the triangles are similar.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: What is the angle between a tangent and the radius at the point of contact?
options: It equals the angle at the centre
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The angle between a tangent and a radius is 90°. Write it with both words, tangent and radius, for the reason mark.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle, centre O. Angle APB = 64°. What is angle AOB?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Angles OAP and OBP are 90° (tangent and radius). The quadrilateral's angles add up to 360°: 360 − 90 − 90 − 64 = 116°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord has length 16 cm. How far is the chord from the centre?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so use half of it: √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6 cm. 12.8 comes from adding the squares.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: An angle at the circumference is 37°. What is the angle at the centre standing on the same arc?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference: 2 × 37 = 74°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Reflex angle AOB at the centre is 250°. C is on the minor arc AB. What is angle ACB?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: With C on the minor arc, angle ACB stands on the major arc, whose angle at the centre is the reflex 250°. Half of it is 125°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is on the circle. Angle CAB = 34°. What is angle CBA?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The angle in a semicircle is 90°, so angle ACB = 90° and angle CBA = 180 − 90 − 34 = 56°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A, B, C and D are on a circle, with C and D on the same side of chord AB. Angle ACB = 48°. What is angle ADB?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Angles in the same segment are equal, so ADB = 48°. 132° would be right only if D were on the other side of AB (cyclic quadrilateral).

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: One angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 112°. What is the opposite angle?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°: 180 − 112 = 68°. Equal opposite angles is a parallelogram property.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Which statement about a cyclic quadrilateral is correct?
options: All four angles add up to 180°
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°. All four add up to 360°, as in any quadrilateral.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A tangent touches a circle at A. The angle between the tangent and the chord AB is 58°. C is on the circle in the alternate segment. What is angle ACB?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Alternate segment theorem: the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment, 58°. 32° is 90 − 58.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: P and Q are on a circle, centre O. QT is the tangent at Q and angle PQT is acute. Angle OPQ = 22°. What is angle PQT?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: OP = OQ (radii), so angle OQP = 22°. Angle OQT = 90° (tangent and radius), so PQT = 90 − 22 = 68°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Chords AB and CD cross at P inside a circle. AP = 4 cm, PB = 9 cm and CP = 6 cm. What is PD?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Intersecting chords: AP × PB = CP × PD, so 36 = 6 × PD and PD = 6 cm. 13.5 puts the pieces in the wrong places (6 × 9 ÷ 4).

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: From a point P outside a circle, one line cuts the circle at A and B with PA = 4 cm and PB = 12 cm. Another cuts it at C and D with PC = 3 cm. What is PD?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: PA × PB = PC × PD, with both distances measured from P: 4 × 12 = 3 × PD, so PD = 16 cm. 10.7 comes from using the chord AB = 8 instead of PB.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Which reason scores the mark for doubling an angle at the circumference?
options: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
Angles in a circle add up to 360°
The angle at the circumference is twice the angle at the centre
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The 2018 1H scheme underlined the key words: angle, centre, twice, circumference. A bare theorem name is not enough, and the last option has it backwards.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A line from the centre O passes through F to D on the circle, with FD = 3 cm. A chord through F has AF × FB = 36. What is the radius?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: The line through O is a diameter. 36 = 3 × FG, so FG = 12 and the diameter is 12 + 3 = 15 cm. The radius is 7.5 cm. Giving 15 is the error the 2018 scheme marked M0A0.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Why is the angle in a semicircle 90°?
options: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°
The tangent meets the radius at 90°
The angle at the centre is 180°, and the angle at the circumference is half of it
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: A diameter makes a straight angle of 180° at the centre. The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre: 90°.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: Two congruent regular pentagons and a regular polygon A fit together exactly at a point. How many sides does A have?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Each pentagon angle is 108°. 360 − 216 = 144° is A's interior angle, so its exterior angle is 36° and it has 360 ÷ 36 = 10 sides.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: The interior angles of a polygon add up to 2340°. How many sides does it have?
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: (n − 2) × 180 = 2340, so n − 2 = 13 and n = 15. 13 forgets to add the 2 back.

09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.q: A reflex angle is an angle
09-angles-polygons-circle-theorems.explain: Acute: less than 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: How many cm² are there in 1 m²?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm². Area conversions square the length factor.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: How many litres are there in 2.5 m³?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: 1 m³ = 1000 litres, so 2.5 m³ = 2500 litres. 2 500 000 is the number of cm³, not litres.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: Convert 450 000 cm² to m².
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: Divide by 10 000: 450 000 ÷ 10 000 = 45 m². Dividing by 100 (the length factor) gives 4500.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A triangle has base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. What is its area?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: ½ × 12 × 7 = 42 cm². 84 forgets the ½.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, 4 cm apart. What is its area?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: ½(a + b)h = ½ × (6 + 10) × 4 = 32 cm². 64 forgets the ½.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: What is the circumference of a circle with diameter 10 cm?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: C = πd = π × 10 = 31.4 cm. 78.5 is the area (π × 5²), and 62.8 uses 2π with the diameter.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: What is the area of a circle with radius 6 cm?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: A = πr² = π × 36 = 113 cm². 37.7 is 2πr, the circumference, and 452 squares the diameter.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: What is the perimeter of a semicircle with diameter 8 cm?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: Half the circumference plus the diameter: ½ × π × 8 + 8 = 4π + 8 = 20.6 cm. 12.6 leaves out the straight edge.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A sector has radius 6 cm and angle 60°. What is its arc length?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: Arc = (60/360) × 2π × 6 = 2π = 6.28 cm. 18.8 (6π) uses πr², which gives the sector's area.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A sector has radius 10 cm and angle 72°. What is its area?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: (72/360) × π × 100 = 20π = 62.8 cm². 12.6 is the arc length, and 314 is the whole circle.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A sector has radius 5 cm and angle 90°. What is its perimeter?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: Arc = ¼ × 2π × 5 = 7.85 cm. Perimeter = arc + two radii = 7.85 + 10 = 17.9 cm. 7.85 leaves out both radii.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A sector has angle 30° and area 12π cm². What is its radius?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: (30/360) × πr² = 12π, so r² = 12 × 12 = 144 and r = 12 cm. 144 forgets the square root.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: A prism has cross-sectional area 24 cm² and length 15 cm. What is its volume?
10-mensuration-and-similarity.explain: Volume = area of cross-section × length = 24 × 15 = 360 cm³. 180 wrongly halves, as if it were a triangle formula.

10-mensuration-and-similarity.q: What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm?
